meta.title: Convolutional code + Viterbi decoder: hard vs soft decisions
meta.tools: k = 7, r = ½ encoder and Viterbi decoder (eelab.comms), Monte Carlo over AWGN
meta.summary: Measure the coding gain of the NASA-standard k = 7 rate-½ convolutional code with hard- and soft-decision Viterbi decoding and compare with the union-bound prediction and the classic ~2 dB soft-decision advantage.
meta.problem: The Viterbi algorithm finds the most likely transmitted sequence through a trellis. How much does feeding it analog ('soft') values instead of hard bits help?
meta.theory:
The (171,133) code has free distance d_free = 10. Soft-decision union bound: $P_b\lesssim\sum_d c_d\,Q(\sqrt{2dRE_b/N_0})$ with leading
spectrum terms $c_{10}=36$, $c_{12}=211$, $c_{14}=1404$. Asymptotic coding gain $10\log_{10}(Rd_{free})$ = 7 dB; soft decisions are
worth ≈ 2 dB over hard decisions (the information lost by quantising to 1 bit).
meta.method: 20,000 information bits per E_b/N₀ point; BPSK over AWGN; hard decoding uses ±1 of the sign, soft uses the raw values.

rows.quantity: Soft Viterbi BER at 3 dB vs union bound
rows.note: the bound is an upper bound
